patient.name: Arjun Mehta
patient.presenting_event: Fell backwards from a low step onto the dorsum of his flexed left wrist 2 hours ago.

history.chief_complaint: Pain and volar wrist deformity, pain 8/10.
history.mechanism: Fall onto a flexed left wrist; not a classic extended-wrist FOOSH.

inspection: Closed distal wrist swelling with volar contour deformity
palpation: No isolated scaphoid or elbow tenderness
neurovascular: Intact median, radial and ulnar sensation and motor screening

learning_objective: Interpret volar displacement, recognize reduction failure and escalate appropriately rather than forcing a routine casting pathway.

history.message: Focus on the injury mechanism, neurovascular symptoms, wounds and other associated injuries. Fall onto a flexed left wrist; not a classic extended-wrist FOOSH.

examination.message: Start with these case-specific findings: Warm hand, capillary refill 2 seconds. Intact median, radial and ulnar sensation and motor screening. Red flag: Progressive median nerve symptoms.

investigations.message: Select investigations that will change management. Initial priority: Left wrist PA and lateral radiographs. Is the distal radius angulated toward the palm or the back of the hand?

diagnosis.message: A volarly displaced extra-articular distal radius fracture after a fall onto a flexed wrist is not a Colles fracture.

treatment.message: Smith pattern. Attempt safe reduction under qualified staff, reassess films; persistent displacement prompts orthopedic fixation planning.
